# SFCmodeler


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

## Usage

### Installation

``` sh
$ pip install SFCmodeler
```

or from [conda](https://anaconda.org/slevey087/SFCmodeler)

``` sh
$ conda install -c slevey087 SFCmodeler
```

Install latest from the GitHub [repository](https://github.com/slevey087/SFCmodeler):

``` sh
$ pip install git+https://github.com/slevey087/SFCmodeler.git
```

Then import with

``` py
from SFCmodeler import *
```

### Documentation

Documentation can be found hosted on this GitHub [repository](https://github.com/slevey087/SFCmodeler)’s [pages](https://slevey087.github.io/SFCmodeler/). Additionally you can find package manager specific guidelines on [conda](https://anaconda.org/slevey087/SFCmodeler) and [pypi](https://pypi.org/project/SFCmodeler/) respectively.

## How to use

First declare `Parameters` (fixed exogenous values) and `Variables` (found endogenously by the solver), each with a `name`, and optional `description` and `initial_value`

``` python
Variable.default_value = 10  # This sets a default initial value for Variables

C = Variable("C","Consumption")
T = Variable("T","Taxes")
V = Variable("V","Wealth",100)   # The number 100 overrides the default value declared above
Y = Variable("Y","GDP")

alpha1 = Parameter("alpha_1","MPC out of income",0.6)
alpha2 = Parameter("alpha_2","MPC out of wealth",0.4)
G = Parameter("G","Government spending",5)
theta = Parameter("theta","Tax rate",0.2)
```

Next define the [`SFCmodel`](https://slevey087.github.io/SFCmodeler/modeler.html#sfcmodel) with a list of equations. Each equation should have one variable on the LHS, then `<<` as the equals sign, then any valid `Sympy` expression:

``` python
model = SFCmodel(
    [
        C << alpha1 * (Y - T) + alpha2 * V(-1),
        Y << C + G,
        T << theta * Y,
        V << V(-1) + Y - T - C
    ]
)
```

Run `.solve()` to solve one period forward, or specify a number of periods to solve more than one time step, and then manipulate the results using `.data`:

``` python
model.solve(10)

model.data
```
